headline: High: shared filesystem and broad tool/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP; next-ai-draw-io ingests files and natural-language commands. Their shared filesystem bridge makes attacker-controlled content in one agent’s outputs plausibly reinterpreted as instructions by the other, though no direct shared channel beyond files is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF one agent writes untrusted content that the other later parses as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files
Require provenance labels on inter-agent files
Review any file passed from A to B before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, images, and text files and calls multiple model APIs. With shared filesystem state, sensitive artifacts can flow from A into B’s outputs or third-party API calls in default workflows, even though the exact leakage path is indirect.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace files
IF sensitive code, screenshots, PDFs, or keys are present in that workspace
IF B forwards file contents to an external model API
mitigations: Use separate least-privilege workspaces
Remove secrets from shared directories
Disable external API routing for sensitive files
Audit which files B uploads before use
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-class access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and MCP use, and Cline additionally has filesystem write and git modification. The pair can concurrently mutate shared workspace state without any documented locking, so conflicting writes, git corruption, or overwritten artifacts are plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same repository or workspace
IF either agent writes files or git state while the other is active
mitigations: Assign one agent per workspace
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce code, browser-derived content, and tool outputs; next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization. If B consumes A’s output without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect diagrams or actions. The pathway is inferred from documented tool use, not directly observed end-to-end.
conditions: IF B treats A-generated text or files as authoritative
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted between A and B
mitigations: Insert a review step between agents
Require citations or source links in A outputs
Have B summarize before acting
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add verification gates and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, images, and text files and can send data to multiple external model providers. The pair creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch and third-party disclosure risk, but no specific jurisdictional violation is documented, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed in the shared workspace
IF B routes those files to external model providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Disable external model routing for sensitive files
Set short retention on uploaded artifacts
Document data-class handling rules for both agents
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
